valuation_philosophy: CMC is a mature, cyclical NZ automotive dealership group (Ford/Mazda anchor plus Southpac trucks, Agricentre tractors and a growing BYD footprint) that also carries a large owned freehold property portfolio on its balance sheet. A pure owner-FCF Gordon-growth DCF materially understates this business: reported and owner FCF are dominated by working-capital swings in vehicle inventory/floorplan financing (FY2016-25 FCF ranged from -$57.1m to +$50.6m with no trend) and by a recent property development supercycle (Fagan Motors rebuild, Avon City Ford, Southpac Palmerston North, Hutchinson Detroit Place) that depressed FCF via elevated capex without reducing true earning power. A reference owner-FCF DCF is disclosed below (base case IV ~$1.54, an obvious under-value versus a $6.85 share price and NZ$9.39 book value) precisely to demonstrate why it is the wrong primary tool here. The PRIMARY valuation instead blends (60% weight) an exit-P/E model on mid-cycle, through-the-cycle trading earnings (NPAT normalized for the FY2024 one-off deferred-tax charge) discounted at cost of equity, with (40% weight) a book-value-compounding / exit-P/B cross-check that anchors to the group's NZ$9.39/share NTA and its 0.73-1.38x historical P/B trading range. This blended approach is the conventional way sell-side and value investors underwrite dealership groups and REIT-like asset-backed cyclicals (see also CDI.NZ, ARG.NZ, SUM.NZ in this research library). The result is an honest, unglamorous conclusion: CMC is a modestly undervalued income-and-asset stock (base case ~+6% to fair value, weighted ~+10%), not a multi-bagger growth story. The stock's real attraction is a well-covered dividend (35cps FY2025, ~5.1% yield at $6.85), a freehold property base providing a hard asset floor, and a currently-depressed 0.73x P/B versus a 10yr average of 1.07x, set against a genuine cyclical recovery already visible in H1-2026 (+50% trading profit after tax YoY).

inputs.shares_outstanding_note: Constant 32,694,632 for the entire FY2016-H1FY2026 history. No buybacks, no options/SBC scheme.
inputs.total_debt_broad_note: FY2025 broad TotalDebt as reported/parsed: Bank Borrowings (current 26.546 + non-current 44.180 = 70.726) + At Call Deposits 28.074 + Vehicle Floorplan Finance 92.451 + Credit Contracts 0.166 + Lease Liabilities 24.177. Reconciles exactly to CSV TotalDebt 215.594.
inputs.net_debt_structural_note: DCF valuation net-debt bridge uses a NARROWER, economically-motivated definition: Bank Borrowings (70.726) + At Call Deposits (28.074, a depositor-scheme funding liability owed to third parties) + Lease Liabilities (24.177, capitalised IFRS16 obligations) minus Cash (11.996) = 110.981. EXCLUDED: Vehicle Floorplan Finance (92.451) and Credit Contracts (0.166), because the company's own FY2020 annual report states plainly that 'property [is] funded by retained earnings and inventory funded by short term borrowing' - floorplan is inventory-secured, self-liquidating financing that revolves 1:1 against a $242.2m vehicle inventory asset, not structural leverage against the going-concern business or fixed assets. At-call deposits, while also deployed into working capital, remain a genuine third-party interest-bearing liability independent of any specific vehicle, so are kept in net debt as a conservative treatment.
inputs.net_debt_broad_for_sanity_check_note: Broad TotalDebt (215.594) minus cash (11.996), used ONLY for the Step 8c implied-EV/EBITDA sanity check so it is apples-to-apples with the user-supplied historical EV/EBITDA series (which was computed on the full broad TotalDebt basis). NOT used in the DCF equity bridge itself.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Reported FCF is NOT used as the DCF base - it is wildly volatile (FY2016-25: +30.8, +1.8, -26.2, +20.3, +50.6, +6.0, +44.7, -35.2, -57.1, +33.6) driven by vehicle inventory/floorplan working-capital swings, not economics.
inputs.sbc_source: Verified NIL - filings disclose no share-based payment scheme across all periods FY2016-H1FY2026. Explicitly zero, not missing/unavailable.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income is immaterial across all periods (e.g. FY2016 $0.18m, FY2020 $0.006m) - no material net cash pile, so no strip-out required. CMC is a net-debt company.
inputs.capex_data_caveat: CapEx for FY2021-FY2025 and all half-years is a PROXY: net investing cash outflow, not gross PP&E purchases, because CMC's annual reports switched to a concise format from FY2021 that discloses only net investing cash flow. FY2020 cross-check: net capex 13.244 vs gross capex 13.626 (proxy understates true capex by ~2.8%). All forward capex-as-%-of-revenue assumptions in this model implicitly inherit this small understatement; a +3% gross-up was applied when deriving the earnings-based mid-cycle FCF cross-check figure.
inputs.fy2024_npat_distortion: FY2024 statutory NetIncome (4.535m, EPS 0.139) includes a -$12.7m one-off non-cash deferred tax charge (removal of tax depreciation on commercial buildings). Trading profit after tax that year was ~$17.9m (trading EPS ~54.7c). FY2024 statutory NPAT/EPS is normalized to $17.9m / $0.547 wherever used as a CAGR endpoint or mid-cycle input in this model; the raw statutory figure is never used directly as a base year.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGRs (3yr -17.9%, 5yr -3.4%) diverge sharply from equity CAGR (5yr +6.2%) and revenue CAGR (5yr +5.8%). This divergence is an artifact of the FY2024 deferred-tax one-off depressing statutory EPS mid-series, plus FY2022 being a cyclical (Clean Car Discount-aided) demand peak used as the 3yr start point - it does NOT reflect a genuine earnings decline trend. Equity/book-value CAGR is structurally the most reliable driver here because it nets out both effects (retained trading earnings net of dividends, smoothed by the 62-65% payout ratio).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGR is not computable/meaningful: reported and owner FCF (SBC=0, so identical) cross zero multiple times across FY2016-2025 (e.g. FY2018 -26.2, FY2023 -35.2, FY2024 -57.1) driven by vehicle inventory/floorplan working-capital timing, not an underlying growth or decline trend. A mid-cycle FCF base was used instead of an endpoint CAGR (see fcf_quality reconciliation below and mid_cycle_fcf_derivation).

mid_cycle_fcf_derivation.purpose: Cross-check for the reference owner-FCF DCF and for sanity-checking the component-built projections, per the explicit data caveat that a single-year FCF base is a trap in this business.

earnings_based_approach.formula: Mean normalized NPAT (FY21-25, FY24 restated to $17.9m trading profit after tax) + mean D&A (FY21-25) - mean maintenance CapEx (FY21-25, grossed up ~3% for the net-investing-outflow proxy)

mid_cycle_fcf_derivation.selected_mid_cycle_owner_fcf_note: Average of earnings-based approach (12.63) and 10yr median reported FCF (13.12) - the two independent methods converge within 4% of each other, a strong cross-check. Used only as a sanity anchor; the reference FCF-DCF instead uses a full 5yr component build (see projections.base) which produces year-1 owner FCF of 17.9 (close to, and slightly above, this mid-cycle anchor as it reflects the ongoing cyclical recovery already visible in H1-2026).

base.wc_capture_note: NEGATIVE capture: unlike a subscription/prepaid business, revenue growth CONSUMES working capital here (inventory build funded against floorplan), so it is a cash drag, not a tailwind.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: Flat NZ statutory rate - the FY2024 distortion was a balance-sheet deferred-tax revaluation, not a cash tax rate anomaly, so no ramp is required.

bull.narrative: OCR-driven cyclical recovery sustains beyond FY2026, BYD/Chinese-EV representation (Adventure Motors, Energy Motors) scales successfully and offsets Ford/Ranger share erosion, Southpac truck cycle turns, rural/agribusiness tailwind persists.

bear.narrative: H1-2026 recovery proves a fickle December/seasonal effect as management cautioned; Chinese OEM (BYD/GWM/MG, already 26.2% of July 2026 passenger registrations) erosion of Ford/Ranger share accelerates faster than CMC's own BYD dealerships can offset; Southpac heavy-truck weakness persists; weak NZD and 2026 model-change disruption (Ranger Super Duty, Mazda 6e/CX-6e) weigh on margins.

small_cap_illiquidity_tightly_held_regis.reason: Market cap ~NZ$224m at $6.85 (below the $300m small-cap illiquidity threshold); Gibbons family holds >60% of shares, leaving a thin free float, low trading liquidity and limited scope for institutional accumulation or index inclusion.

ford_ranger_franchise_concentration.reason: 12 of ~19+ dealership outlets are Ford; Ranger has been central to group profitability for a decade; the franchise itself is owned by Ford, not CMC. Ranger's light-commercial 'sweet spot' fell 18.4% in FY2025, and Chinese OEM brands (BYD, GWM, MG etc.) reached 26.2% of NZ passenger registrations in July 2026, more than double a year earlier, directly threatening this concentration.

nz_vehicle_market_cyclicality.reason: New-vehicle demand is highly discretionary and rate-sensitive (management's own 'two-speed economy' framing). Moderate, not extreme, premium: 10yr EBITDA peak-to-trough is only 1.68x ($37.2m FY2016 to $62.5m FY2023), well short of the >3x threshold that would warrant the full 1.5-2.5% structural-cyclicality premium.

owned_freehold_property_portfolio.reason: A large owned freehold property portfolio (PP&E ~$258-284m carrying value, $117.6m property revaluation reserve embedded in equity) backs the balance sheet, lowers financial/downside risk relative to a pure asset-light dealership peer, and gives CMC flexibility (develop, sell, relocate) most competitors lack. This is explicitly NOT over-penalized in the cyclicality/illiquidity premiums above.

wacc_rationale.bull_wacc_note: 1.5pp below base - bull case assumes successful execution reduces franchise-concentration and cyclicality risk premiums (BYD diversification succeeds, cycle turns favourably).
wacc_rationale.bear_wacc_note: 2.0pp above base - bear case assumes the Ford/Chinese-OEM competitive risk and truck-segment weakness both crystallize as structural, compounding, non-diversifiable risks.

valuation_methodology: Blended model: 60% weight on an exit-P/E model (mid-cycle NPAT projected 5yr, exit multiple applied to Year-5 NPAT, discounted at cost of equity, plus PV of interim dividends), 40% weight on a book-value-compounding / exit-P/B model (BVPS compounded forward at a through-cycle equity growth rate, exit P/B applied in Year 5, discounted at cost of equity, plus PV of the same interim dividends). A reference owner-FCF Gordon-growth DCF is also computed and disclosed (see valuation.base_fcf_reference) but is NOT part of the blended IV - it is included to show why a pure FCF-DCF understates this property-backed, working-capital-heavy dealership group.

fcf_reference_dcf.note: NOT used in blended IV - reference only, demonstrates why pure FCF-Gordon understates this business

entry_price.methodology: PV of base-case interim dividends (Yr1-5) at 15% + PV of blended (60% exit-P/E / 40% exit-P/B) Year-5 exit equity value at 15%, divided by shares outstanding (flat, no dilution). Distributions only are added on top of the exit value (retained earnings are already embedded in the BVPS-compounding half of the blend), per the skill's guidance for non-FCF/book-value models.

sensitivity.basis: Exit-P/E model (primary valuation driver), base-case NPAT path. WACC/CoE +/-2%, terminal-growth-driven exit P/E ladder +/-1pp anchored at 11.1x @ 2.0% (per Gordon-relationship, dPE/dg increasing with g).

sanity_check.implied_multiples_basis_note: Implied P/E and P/B computed on base-case blended intrinsic value ($7.25) against FY2025 actuals (EPS $0.561, BVPS $9.39). Implied EV/EBITDA uses the BROAD net-debt basis ($203.6m) for apples-to-apples comparability with the user-supplied historical EV/EBITDA series, which was also computed on the full broad TotalDebt.

historical_averages_ex_outliers.pe_note: FY2024 (49.2x) excluded as a deferred-tax-driven outlier

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Implied P/E (12.9x) sits modestly above the 11.1x ex-outlier historical average but well inside the 2.0x threshold (22.2x) and below the historical max (13.1x, FY2019). Implied P/B (0.77x) is essentially at the current market multiple (0.73x) and well within the 0.73-1.38x historical range. Implied EV/EBITDA (8.6x) sits within the 6.4-9.4x historical band. Base case upside is a modest 5.8% (well under the 100% trip threshold), consistent with a fairly-valued to modestly-undervalued mature cyclical, not an extrapolated growth story. This clean pass is itself evidence that the deliberate pivot away from a pure FCF-Gordon DCF (which produced an obviously-wrong base-case IV of $1.54, a >1.5x understatement even versus the historical P/B floor) toward the blended earnings+asset approach was the correct methodological choice for this business.
sanity_check.fix_applied: None required - methodology was chosen deliberately upfront (blended exit-P/E + exit-P/B given the mid-cycle-FCF/property-backed data caveats), rather than needing correction after a failed pure-FCF-DCF run. The FCF-DCF's failure (IV $1.54, 77% below the blended model) is disclosed as valuation.base.fcf_reference_dcf precisely so a future reader can see the methodology choice was load-bearing.
